## THE FULFILMENT CONVEYOR BELT (4.1)

### Purpose
Only way to scale agency/coaching to $1M/mo = consistent, repeatable, scalable fulfilment. At scale, fulfilment becomes a profit center through retention + ascension → increased LTV → combats rising ad costs.

### 4-Stage Build Process

| Stage | Focus | Outcome |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 1 | Define deliverables through 20-30 client iteration loop | Know: exact deliverables, implementation methods, most efficient sequence |
| 2 | Build CRM pipeline (100K-foot view stages only) + client cards | Visual conveyor belt with "doctor's file" per client |
| 3 | Document SOPs/checklists for each stage | System replaces founder as the "glue" |
| 4 | Install AMs into the proven belt | Founder transitions from clients → managing team |

### SCIO Pipeline Stages (Exact)
Needs OB Material → Booked OB Call → VSL → Ads → Launching Sequence → Launched/Active → Ascended/Offboarded/Refunded

### Client Card Contents (SCIO)
Sales call notes, OB call recording + doc, ad + VSL scripts, creatives (edited + raw), coaching calls, all funnel links, pixel base code. "Doctor's file" analogy — open any client and know everything.

### Key Principle
Same thing, every time, for every client. Any variation kills scalability. SCIO refined for all of 2022 before reaching "blindly take a client through to results" level.

## THE ACCOUNT MANAGER MODEL (4.2)

### Why This Model
1. Clients get real SMEs (not junior reps)
2. SMEs earn $10K-$15K/mo (nowhere else to make that without starting own business)
3. Enables 1-on-1/DFY at scale → massively increases LTV, decreases churn, decreases refunds

### AM Responsibilities
- Primary: Move clients through conveyor belt + work 1-on-1
- DFY: Facilitate DFY elements
- KPI'd on: Retention
- Clients think of AM when they think of company

### 3-Stage Team Build

| Stage | What Happens | Founder's Role |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| 1 | Hire 1 AM, dial in capacity/skills/onboarding | Still in direct fulfilment + training (osmosis) |
| 2 | Hire more AMs (2 if volume allows) | Step out of direct fulfilment → manage AMs |
| 3 | Promote top AM to CSD (no clients of own) | Manage CSD who manages AMs |

### CSD Structure
- CSD handles 7 direct reports (AMs)
- Supports 140-245 clients while maintaining quality
- Founder acts as CSD until ~$250K/mo
- Cannot outsource CSD role — must validate both AM + CSD simultaneously
- Attend 1 team call/week (Monday morning) for vision/mission/values

### Asset Creation
AM model creates company asset detached from founder → sellable.

## NEW CLIENT ONBOARDING (4.3)

### Why OB Matters
Client is MOST nervous, apprehensive, impressionable right after purchase. First 5-7 days set trajectory for entire engagement.

### 5-7 Day Target State
1. "I can see the path to success"
2. "I REALLY like who I'm working with"
3. "I have full confidence this is THE team"

### Closer Handover (8 Steps)
1. Set correct expectations on sales call
2. Collect payment + sign contract
3. Get prospect hyped → set up Slack channel immediately while paying
4. Walk through OB funnel step-by-step on-call
5. Manually schedule OB call (proactive)
6. Mention upcoming Loom video
7. Send Loom re-explaining next steps + voice note transferring trust to fulfilment team
8. Post in #new-clients: name, email, doc + voice note (who they are, offer, starting point, goals, struggles)

### Fulfilment Team Handover
- CSM creates channel → introduces self FIRST → adds client
- Whole team piles on introductions using closer's intel
- Relate new client to current client getting great results in same niche
- Push to complete OB funnel + book OB call

### OB Funnel
1. Intro video (sell process, show math, set expectations)
2. Intake form (business insight + tech access)
3. Schedule OB call
4. Any other required access
5. Next steps

### OB Call Flow (60 min)
1. Build rapport (~10 min) — where they're based, family, history
2. Clear basic/tech questions
3. Create pathways to goals (5-6 priorities from intake form)
4. Build productized offer together (20-30 min)
5. Explain next steps with screen share
6. Final questions → end call

### Key Rule
OB calls = LAST thing founder delegates.

## AM MINDSET MODEL (4.4)

### The Exercise
"You've lost all clients but one. No more marketing. The only way to get paid is referrals from this one client."

How would you treat them? What results? What experience? What onboarding?

### The Standard
Treat every single client this way → never make less than $10K/month as an AM.

## PROACTIVE LEADERSHIP (4.5)

### The Rule
If a client EVER asks "what's next?" — you've failed.

### Reactive vs Proactive
- **Reactive** = help desk waiting for messages. Unacceptable.
- **Proactive** = predict what client needs next, reach out BEFORE they ask.

### Analogy
Owner walking the dog (proactive) vs dog dragging the owner (reactive).

### In Practice
- Client finishing a step? Tell them next steps before they ask
- Ads underperforming? Update them + explain fix before they notice
- Ads performing? Proactively communicate what's next
- Always be first

### Guiding Light Principle
Most ad-sourced clients are nervous/uncertain. AMs = guiding light. Sometimes means pushing back on client's reference points with expert perspective.

### ICU Clients
Problem clients needing urgent attention outside normal cadence. Priority response regardless of schedule blocks.

## CLIENT COMMUNICATION FRAMEWORK (4.6)

### Core Value
"Client results and client experience first." Communication = #1 driver AND achilles heel.

### Master Framework: Seek to Understand Before Being Understood
1. **Understand the question** — clarify before answering, never guess
2. **Understand the personality** — direct vs wants to feel cared for
3. **Understand how they're feeling** — most important factor, read cues, tailor delivery

### 4 Communication Frameworks

| Framework | When | Structure |
|-----------|------|-----------|
| General | Updates/status | What's going on → what we're doing → next steps |
| Question Answering | Client asks something | Clarify → understand WHY asking → answer both question AND deeper reason |
| Difficult Feedback | Bad news/pushback | What's going on → doing → next steps → WHY → proactively acknowledge emotions |
| Getting Tasks Done | Client needs to act | THAT (communicate + repeat) → WHY (tie to goals) → HOW (training/clarity) |

### Best Practices
Be precise, don't ramble, think from client's perspective, make outcome of every message clear. If can't self-assess in real-time, rewatch/relisten before sending.

## AM DAILY SCHEDULE (4.6 + 4.7)

### 5-Block Structure

| Block | Duration | Focus |
|-------|----------|-------|
| 1 | 60 min | Client comms — respond to all overnight messages (VNs/Looms), drop calendar links |
| 2 | 2 hrs | Deep work — copy, VSL reviews |
| 3 | 1 hr | Client comms — respond to replies, provide updates, deliver reviews |
| 4 | 4 hrs | Deep work — ads (track results, check accounts, launch new clients) |
| 5 | 60 min | Final client comms — every client up to date, next steps clear, metrics communicated, EOD report |

### Real Schedule (From 4.7 AM Walkthrough)
8:30 AM start → client comms (1-1.5hr) → copy deep work (2hr) → client comms (1hr) → ads deep work (4hr) → client comms (1hr) → EOD report → (unofficial) call slots for timezone accommodation → 12AM team call → final client comm block for US/Australian clients

### Key Numbers
- 1 call/day with clients → ~20 calls/month covers most clients
- Schedule prevents "always in Slack" trap at 20-25+ clients
- 7-8 hour structured workday with more productivity than unstructured approach

### ICU Exception
Problem clients monitored throughout day — don't force them to wait for next comm block.

### Adaptability Note
Schedule is SCIO-specific (ads-focused). Deep work blocks change per offer/deliverables. Core structure (3 comm + 2 deep work) transfers universally.

## APW APPLICATION NOTES

### APW Conveyor Belt Stages (Proposed)
Onboard → Assess Fundability → Build/Optimize Credit Profile → Select Funding Route → Apply → Fund → Ascend/Offboard

### APW AM = Funding Specialist
SME in: credit optimization, bank relationships, funding routes, lender requirements, compliance. Must know the field deeply enough to guide nervous clients through unfamiliar territory.

### APW OB Adaptation
- DWY tiers: Automated OB funnel (video → form → community → first module). No 1-on-1 call.
- DFY tiers: 1-on-1 OB call = fundability assessment + path mapping. Founder takes until validated.

### APW Communication Adaptation
- Deep work blocks = application processing, credit optimization, lender research (not ads/copy)
- Proactive leadership especially critical during bank review periods
- ICU clients = time-sensitive funding deadlines, disputed applications, compliance issues
